title_en: Shixin Ronghe Investment Management Co., Ltd. v. Chang'an International Trust Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over trust contract
ruling_gist_en: In a limited partnership, if the managing partner fails to exercise litigation rights, a limited partner who does not manage partnership affairs may bring an action in its own name for the benefit of the partnership.
keywords_en: Civil; Trust contract dispute; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Shaanxi Province; Tianjin; Legal person; Trust Law; Partnership Enterprise Law; Standing to sue of limited partner; Certainty of trust property; Impact of encumbrances on validity of trust; Dismissal of claims; Transfer of stock income rights; Trust plan; Limited partnership investment; Contract dispute; Trust contract dispute with a limited company, etc.
full_text_en:
Shi Xin Rong He Investment Management Co., Ltd. v. Chang'an International Trust Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over trust contract

Ruling Summary

1. In a limited partnership, if the managing partner is inactive in exercising litigation rights, a limited partner who does not execute partnership affairs may bring a lawsuit in its own name for the benefit of the partnership.

2. Upon the establishment of a fund trust, the funds obtained by the trustee from the settlor due to the commitment of trust are trust property; after the establishment of the fund trust, the property acquired by the trustee through the management, use, or disposal of such funds also constitutes trust property.

3. The certainty of trust property is reflected in the property being clear and specific. The certainty of trust property requires that it be segregated and designated from the settlor's own property, and that its quantity and boundaries be clear, so that the trustee can manage, use, and dispose of it for the realization of the trust purpose; the existence of a right burden on the trust property or a third party's purchase right over such property is a different legal issue from the certainty of trust property, and does not necessarily affect the certainty of trust property.

4. A party's claim that the trust is invalid due to the existence of a right burden on the trust property or a third party's purchase right over such property cannot be sustained.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zhong No. 19

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Shi Xin Rong He Investment Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 1110, 11th Floor, Building 3, No. 28 Guandongdian, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhao Chunsheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Meng Qingjun, lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Bao Cuijie, trainee lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Chang'an International Trust Co., Ltd. Domicile: 23rd and 24th Floors, Gaoxin International Business Center, No. 33 Keji Road, High-tech Zone, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Gao Chengcheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Jin, lawyer of Shaanxi Hanting Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Phase I Fund (Limited Partnership). Domicile: Room 4032, 4th Floor, Binhai Financial Street-E2-ABC, No. 20 East Plaza Road, Tianjin Development Zone, Tianjin.

Managing Partner: Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Management Center (Limited Partnership) (Representative: Wu Shangzhi).

Agent ad litem: Lv Yanfeng, lawyer of Beijing Kangda (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Tianjin Dinghui Yuanbo Equity Investment Fund (Limited Partnership). Domicile: Room 4038, 4th Floor, Binhai Financial Street-E2-ABC, No. 20 East Plaza Road, Tianjin Development Zone, Tianjin.

Managing Partner: Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Management Center (Limited Partnership) (Representative: Wu Shangzhi).

Agent ad litem: Lv Yanfeng, lawyer of Beijing Kangda (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at first instance): Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Management Center (Limited Partnership). Domicile: Room 4033, 4th Floor, E2-ABC, Binhai Financial Street, No. 20 East Plaza Road, Tianjin Development Zone, Tianjin.

Managing Partner: Dinghui Equity Investment Management (Tianjin) Co., Ltd. (Representative: Wu Shangzhi).

Agent ad litem: Lv Yanfeng, lawyer of Beijing Kangda (Xi'an) Law Firm.

Third party at first instance: Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng Chengcheng Equity Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership). Domicile: Room AE318, 3rd Floor, Building 6, Binhai Financial Street, No. 52 West Xincheng Road, Tianjin Development Zone, Tianjin.

Managing Partner: Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng Equity Investment Management Co., Ltd. (Representative: Wang Jian).

Agent ad litem: Wang Jian, representative of the partnership.

The appellant Shi Xin Rong He Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shi Xin Rong He) appealed to this Court against the civil judgment of the Shaanxi High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shaanxi High Court) (2015) Shaan Min Er Chu Zi No. 00012, in the case of trust contract dispute with the appellees Chang'an International Trust Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chang'an Trust), Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Phase I Fund (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Dinghui Phase I), Tianjin Dinghui Yuanbo Equity Investment Fund (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Dinghui Yuanbo), Tianjin Dinghui Equity Investment Management Center (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Dinghui Management Center), and the third party at first instance Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng Chengcheng Equity Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Dongfang Gaosheng). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Liu Chongli serving as the presiding judge, and acting judges Li Yulin and Du Jun participating in the trial. Court clerk Sun Dechang served as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The Shaanxi High Court found the following facts upon trial:

From 2010 to 2011, the listed company Century Guanghua Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Century Guanghua) underwent a major asset restructuring, and Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo obtained 11,543,568 shares of "Hengyi Petrochemical" by participating in the restructuring. On April 29, 2010, and December 20, 2010, Century Guanghua signed the "Agreement on Performance Compensation" and the "Supplemental Agreement to the Agreement on Performance Compensation" with the restructuring participants Zhejiang Hengyi Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hengyi Group), Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo, stipulating: if the actual profits of Zhejiang Hengyi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. in each fiscal year of 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013 failed to meet the agreed calculation targets, Century Guanghua could repurchase the shares held by Hengyi Group, Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo at a price of RMB 1 yuan to reduce its registered capital. At the same time, it was agreed that if the performance compensation situation as stipulated in the agreement occurred, Century Guanghua should first repurchase shares from Hengyi Group; when the number of shares held by Hengyi Group was less than the number of shares to be compensated, Century Guanghua would repurchase shares from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo. On May 27, 2011, Century Guanghua issued the "Century Guanghua Technology Co., Ltd. Report on the Implementation of Major Asset Sale and Issuance of Shares to Purchase Assets and Related Party Transactions," confirming: on May 10, 2011, Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo completed the registration of the shares in question and committed not to transfer them within 36 months from the date of registration completion. According to the "Announcement on the Implementation of the Transfer of Shares for Performance Compensation Commitments of Zhejiang Hengyi Group Co., Ltd." issued by Hengyi Petrochemical on May 14, 2014, Hengyi Group ultimately distributed 13,167,295 shares as a stock dividend to shareholders other than the performance compensation committing parties, and after the distribution, Hengyi Group held 70.03% of the shares of "Hengyi Petrochemical."

In August 2011, Shi Xin Rong He signed the "Partnership Agreement" and formed the partnership enterprise Dongfang Gaosheng together with Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng Equity Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng) and other 7 partners. On August 16 of the same year, Dongfang Gaosheng held the first temporary meeting of partners, and all partners unanimously agreed that "the partnership funds shall be used to acquire the share income rights of the restricted tradable shares of Hengyi Petrochemical." On February 15, 2012, Dongfang Gaosheng held the 2012 Investment Decision Committee meeting, which resolved: Chang'an Trust would raise RMB 310 million to purchase the income rights of 9,004,000 shares and 2,539,600 shares (totaling 11,543,600 shares) of Hengyi Petrochemical stocks held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively; it agreed that Dongfang Gaosheng and Chang'an Trust would sign the "Chang'an Trust Gaoshen Phase I Tiered Stock Income Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Contract" and contribute a total of RMB 112 million to subscribe for the trust units issued by Chang'an Trust, with each trust unit having a face value of RMB 1.

On March 15, 2012, Chang'an Trust signed the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively. The main contents of the agreement were: Chang'an Trust planned to raise funds by issuing the "Chang'an Trust Gaoshen Phase I Tiered Stock Income Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Plan" and, using the raised trust funds, acquire from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo the income rights of their restricted tradable shares of Hengyi Petrochemical during the agreed period, subject to the terms and conditions of the agreement. Specifically, it acquired the income rights of 9,003,983 shares held by Dinghui Phase I at a price of RMB 241.8 million, and the income rights of 2,539,585 shares held by Dinghui Yuanbo at a price of RMB 68.2 million. Only after the "Trust Plan" had been formally established would Chang'an Trust be obliged to pay the above transfer consideration to the transferors. The subject stocks had a lock-up period of 3 years, with the lifting of the lock-up date being June 8, 2014. The agreed income period referred to the period from the date when Chang'an Trust paid all transfer considerations to the date when the subject stocks were fully disposed of in accordance with the instructions of Chang'an Trust after the lock-up period expired. The stock income rights included the disposal income from the stocks and the dividends, bonus shares, rights issues, new share warrants, and other fruits actually obtained during the agreed income period; shareholder rights other than the above income rights, such as voting rights, supervision rights, and information rights, were to continue to be exercised by the transferors. After Chang'an Trust had paid the full transfer price, the transferors authorized Chang'an Trust, after the lock-up period expired, to instruct the custodian of the subject stocks, Guosen Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guosen Securities), to legally dispose of the subject stocks, and to instruct the depository bank, Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank), to transfer the proceeds from the disposal of the subject stocks to Chang'an Trust. On the same day, to ensure the performance of the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement," Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively signed the "Stock Custody Service and Commitment Agreement" with Guosen Securities, agreeing to custody the subject stocks at a designated seat of Guosen Securities and not to change or cancel their securities accounts at Guosen Securities without authorization, nor to cancel the designation or transfer custody of the securities accounts, nor to change the third-party depository bank accounts without authorization; Chang'an Trust respectively signed the "Tripartite Operation and Supervision Agreement" with Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank, Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo, designating Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank as the depository bank, and Chang'an Trust had the right to transfer the income from the subject stocks to its own account through that bank; Chang'an Trust also signed the "Stock Pledge Contract" with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively, pledging the subject stocks to Chang'an Trust to secure the performance of the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement," and the corresponding securities pledge registration was completed on March 26 of the same year.

On March 28, 2012, Dongfang Gaosheng signed two "Risk Disclosure Statements for Subscription" and the corresponding "Chang'an Trust Gaoshen Phase I Tiered Stock Income Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Trust Contract"). In the "Risk Disclosure Statement for Subscription," Chang'an Trust informed investors: the trust plan did not guarantee principal protection and minimum returns and involved certain investment risks; the subscriber read and understood all trust documents and was willing to bear the corresponding trust investment risks in accordance with the law before voluntarily subscribing to the corresponding trust units. Article 13 of the Trust Contract, "Special Obligations of Subordinate Settlors and Subordinate Beneficiaries," provided: The funds added by the subordinate settlor were divided into Category A funds and Category B funds. Provisions for adding Category A funds: during the trust term, at the end of the 10th month of each trust year, if the trust property in cash was insufficient to pay the custody fees, trust remuneration, and investment advisory fees payable for that year, the subordinate settlor was obliged to add the shortfall to the trust in cash. The trustee would then issue a reminder letter to the subordinate settlor in writing to add funds. If the subordinate settlor failed to add sufficient funds within 30 days after the trustee issued the reminder letter, the subordinate beneficiary would be deemed to have waived the beneficial rights to all its trust units, and the subordinate beneficial rights under this trust would belong to the priority settlor; Provisions for adding Category B funds: during the trust term, the trustee monitored the market daily and set the addition line for Category B funds for the stocks invested under this trust at RMB 27.56. During the trust term, the trustee had the right to adjust the addition line for Category B funds under this trust. During the trust term, if the closing price of the subject stocks on day T was higher than the addition line, the trust plan would operate normally. If the closing price of the stocks on day T during the trust term fell to or below the addition line, the trustee should notify the subordinate beneficiary by fax or telephone before 10:00 a.m. on day T+1. The subordinate beneficiary had the right to decide whether to add funds or stocks after receiving the notice. If the subordinate beneficiary added funds or stocks, the added funds or stocks should be included in the trust property so that the total value of the trust assets recovered to a level above [holding stocks x addition line]. If the closing price of the subject stocks on day T fell to or below the addition line, and the subordinate beneficiary failed to add funds or stocks promptly within T+5 days, or if the total value of the trust property did not recover to a level above [holding stocks x addition line] on day T+5, the subordinate beneficiary would be deemed to have waived the beneficial rights to all its trust units, and the subordinate beneficial rights under this trust would belong to the priority settlor. Article 16 "Risk Disclosure," paragraph (1), subparagraph 8 stipulated: The trust plan adopted a structured design, and the ordinary beneficiary and subordinate beneficiary guaranteed the principal and income of the priority beneficiary with their funds participating in the trust plan. The risks borne by the ordinary beneficiary and subordinate beneficiary were far greater than those borne by the priority beneficiary. During the operation of the trust property, there might be a risk of total loss of the subscription funds paid by the ordinary beneficiary and subordinate beneficiary due to a decline in the price of the subject stocks. According to the provisions of the two Trust Contracts, the third party subscribed for 25.09 million ordinary trust units and 86.95 million subordinate trust units, with total subscription funds of RMB 112.04 million. Dongfang Gaosheng paid the above subscription funds in full to Chang'an Trust on the date of signing. Chang'an Trust and Dongfang Gaosheng also signed the "Supplemental Agreement to the Gaoshen Phase I Tiered Stock Income Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Plan Trust Contract," changing the subscription of 86.95 million yuan for subordinate trust units to 86.91 million yuan. The excess 40,000 yuan paid was not included in the trust property and did not constitute trust units held by Dongfang Gaosheng; instead, 31,000 yuan was used to pay notarization fees, and the remaining 9,000 yuan was returned to Dongfang Gaosheng. Ultimately, the amount of subscription funds delivered by Dongfang Gaosheng to Chang'an Trust was RMB 112,031,000. On August 27, 2012, the subject stock "Hengyi Petrochemical" triggered the early warning line due to prolonged market decline, and Chang'an Trust notified Dongfang Gaosheng to add margin. On August 31, 2012, Dongfang Gaosheng added Category B margin of RMB 1,385,200. On March 7, 2013, it added Category A margin of RMB 6,065,800. On March 1, 2013, Chang'an Trust sent a consultation letter to the third party Dongfang Gaosheng, the main content of which was: As the subordinate beneficiary of the trust plan, at the request of all beneficiaries, you are now to convene a beneficiary meeting by correspondence to vote on the following matters: (1) agree to amend Article 10 of the Trust Contract; (2) agree to amend Article 11 of the Trust Contract; (3) agree to amend the second part of Article 13 of the Trust Contract, "Provisions for Adding Category B Funds," from "If the closing price of the subject stocks on day T falls to or below the addition line, and the subordinate beneficiary fails to add funds or stocks promptly within T+5 days, or if the total value of the trust property does not recover to a level above [holding stocks x addition line] on day T+5, the subordinate beneficiary shall be deemed to have waived the beneficial rights to all its trust units, and the subordinate beneficial rights under this trust shall belong to the priority settlor" to "If the closing price of the subject stocks on day T falls to or below the addition line, and the subordinate beneficiary fails to add funds or stocks promptly within T+5 days, or if the total value of the trust property does not recover to a level above [holding stocks x addition line] on day T+5, or fails to provide credit enhancement through an institution with a public market main body credit rating of AA-level (or above) as required by the priority beneficiary, the subordinate beneficiary shall be deemed to have waived the beneficial rights to all its trust units, and the subordinate beneficial rights under this trust shall belong to the priority settlor." If there was any conflict between the content of this consultation letter and the original contract, the consultation letter would prevail. The trustee, in accordance with the trust document provisions, sought your opinion on the above adjustment to decide whether to implement it. Dongfang Gaosheng sealed and agreed to the above adjustment plan. In October 2014, after the lock-up period of the subject stocks expired, due to the continuous decline in the price of the subject stocks, on September 26, 2014, the priority trust unit Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank issued an instruction letter to Chang'an Trust, the main content of which was: The subject stock "Hengyi Petrochemical" was unlocked on July 16, 2014, the closing price of the subject stocks continued to be lower than the priority principal-protected price, and the subordinate beneficiary had not yet added cash or stocks. Therefore, in accordance with the provisions of the "Consultation Letter," the priority beneficiary, i.e., this bank, requested that your company immediately liquidate the holding stocks and use the proceeds to repay the principal and interest of the priority beneficiary. On October 11, 2014, Chang'an Trust issued a notice to Dongfang Gaosheng, the main content of which was: In accordance with the provisions of the "Consultation Letter" approved by the beneficiary meeting on March 1, 2013, the stock "Hengyi Petrochemical" under this trust plan was unlocked on July 16, 2014, the closing price of the subject stocks continued to be lower than the priority principal-protected price, and the subordinate beneficiary had not yet added cash or stocks. The priority beneficiary had issued an instruction letter to Chang'an Trust to liquidate the holding stocks, and Chang'an Trust, in accordance with the provisions of the "Consultation Letter," would proceed to liquidate the holding stocks. Subsequently, on October 13 and 21, Chang'an Trust lifted the pledge registration of the subject stocks and sold them all. On October 27, Chang'an Trust distributed and settled the proceeds from the sale of the subject stocks, totaling RMB 185,141,010.31. Since the trust property was insufficient to fully pay the principal and income of the priority beneficiary at the time of settlement, the subordinate beneficiary Dongfang Gaosheng received zero distribution. Chang'an Trust publicly issued the "Chang'an Trust Gaoshen Phase I Tiered Stock Income Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Plan Liquidation Report" and declared: If the settlor and beneficiary did not raise a written objection within 3 business days from the date of the announcement of the "Liquidation Report," Chang'an Trust would be released from responsibility for the contents listed in the liquidation report. Within the objection period, neither Shi Xin Rong He nor Dongfang Gaosheng raised any objection to Chang'an Trust regarding the liquidation. On March 5, 2015, Shi Xin Rong He sent a "Request for Rights Protection Urgent Letter" by mail to Dongfang Gaosheng and Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng, stating that Chang'an Trust had maliciously colluded with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, causing its entire trust investment loss, and requesting that Dongfang Gaosheng and Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng immediately take action to file a lawsuit with the court. On March 31, Tianjin Dongfang Gaosheng replied, stating that it had engaged a lawyer to study the relevant documents but had not yet obtained evidence of malicious collusion between Chang'an Trust and Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, expressing hope that Shi Xin Rong He could provide assistance.

Shixin Ronghe Company, in accordance with the provisions of the Partnership Agreement and Article 68 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC, filed a lawsuit with the Shaanxi High People's Court, requesting: 1. A judgment declaring the two Trust Contracts signed between Chang'an Trust and Dongfang Gaosheng null and void; 2. An order compelling Chang'an Trust to return the subscription funds of 112,031,000 yuan to Dongfang Gaosheng, plus the additional margin of 6,065,814 yuan paid under the Trust Contracts, totaling 118,096,814 yuan; 3. An order compelling Chang'an Trust to compensate Dongfang Gaosheng for interest losses calculated at the benchmark lending rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, amounting to 21,693,166.45 yuan (interest on the subscription funds calculated from the payment date March 28, 2012 to March 30, 2015, totaling 20,737,858.91 yuan; interest on the additional margin calculated from the payment date September 1, 2012 to March 30, 2015, totaling 955,307.54 yuan, with interest losses to be calculated until the actual date of payment); 4. An order that Chang'an Trust bear the litigation costs of the case; 5. An order that Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Dinghui Management Center bear joint and several liability with Chang'an Trust.

The Shaanxi High People's Court found at trial that the disputed issues in the case were: 1. Whether Shixin Ronghe Company, as a partner of Dongfang Gaosheng, had the right to file the lawsuit; 2. Whether the Trust Contracts signed between Chang'an Trust and Dongfang Gaosheng were valid.

Regarding the first disputed issue, the court held that Shixin Ronghe Company had the right to file the lawsuit. Pursuant to Article 68 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC, when the managing partner fails to exercise its rights, a limited partner may urge it to do so or, in the interest of the enterprise, file a lawsuit in its own name. After Shixin Ronghe Company believed that the rights of the partnership enterprise Dongfang Gaosheng had been infringed, it sent a letter of demand to Dongfang Gaosheng and the managing partner, urging Dongfang Gaosheng to file a civil lawsuit in the people's court to protect its civil rights. Although Dongfang Gaosheng responded, it did not file a civil lawsuit in accordance with the law. Shixin Ronghe Company then chose to file a lawsuit in its own name, which was not improper and complied with legal provisions. Chang'an Trust's defense that Dongfang Gaosheng had not failed to exercise its rights and that the condition for Shixin Ronghe Company to file a lawsuit in its own name was not satisfied did not comply with legal provisions, and the court did not accept it.

Regarding the second disputed issue, the court held that the Trust Contracts signed between Chang'an Trust and Dongfang Gaosheng represented the true intentions of both parties, their content did not violate legal provisions, and they should be valid and legal contracts. Shixin Ronghe Company's argument that the subject matter of the trust contracts was uncertain and therefore the contracts should be null and void was contrary to the facts and the law. First, Chang'an Trust established the Gaosheng Phase I Tiered Stock Earnings Rights Investment Collective Fund Trust Plan at the proposal of Dongfang Gaosheng. In August 2011, Shixin Ronghe Company and other partners signed the Partnership Agreement to form the partnership enterprise Dongfang Gaosheng, in which Shixin Ronghe Company held a 25.42% share. On August 16 of the same year, Dongfang Gaosheng held its first temporary partners' meeting, where all partners unanimously agreed that "the partnership funds shall be used to acquire the earnings rights of the restricted shares of Hengyi Petrochemical." On February 15, 2012, Dongfang Gaosheng held the 2012 Investment Decision Committee meeting, resolving that Chang'an Trust would raise 310 million yuan to purchase the stock earnings rights of 9.004 million shares and 2.5396 million shares (totaling 11.5436 million shares) of "Hengyi Petrochemical" held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively; and agreeing that Dongfang Gaosheng and Chang'an Trust would sign the Trust Contracts, with Dongfang Gaosheng subscribing a total of 112 million yuan to purchase trust units issued by Chang'an Trust, with each trust unit having a face value of 1 yuan. It was only then that Chang'an Trust, on March 15, 2012, signed the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, which explicitly stipulated that Chang'an Trust's obligation to pay the transfer price to the transferors would arise only after the "Trust Plan" had been formally established. Chang'an Trust acquired the earnings rights of the "Hengyi Petrochemical" shares held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, thereby obtaining the subject matter of the trust contracts. Therefore, the establishment of this Trust Contract project was at the request of Dongfang Gaosheng; only after the trust plan was established would Chang'an Trust pay the transfer price to Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo to purchase the trust subject matter. The investigation and understanding of whether the earnings rights of the "Hengyi Petrochemical" shares under the Trust Contracts could be invested in was completed by Dongfang Gaosheng, which ultimately decided on the investment. As the largest partner of Dongfang Gaosheng, Shixin Ronghe Company should have been fully informed and aware of the content of the investment project. Now that the project has suffered losses, Shixin Ronghe Company's attempt to deny the validity of the contracts on the ground that the trust subject matter was uncertain is contrary to the principle of good faith in commercial dealings. Therefore, the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement signed by Chang'an Trust with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo for the purpose of establishing the Trust Contracts also did not violate legal provisions and should be valid. Shixin Ronghe Company's request that Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo bear joint and several liability lacked both legal and factual basis, and the court did not support it. Second, Shixin Ronghe Company's argument that at the time of signing, the subject shares were still within the performance compensation period and were in a state where they could be repurchased by the listed company, rendering the earnings rights of the subject shares uncertain and the trust contracts invalid, was inconsistent with the facts of the case. The uncertainty regarding the shares did not materialize during the entire execution period of the trust plan, and the trust contracts were not affected by this uncertainty in their normal execution. Shixin Ronghe Company's attempt to deny the validity of the contracts based on a possible event was contrary to the law. In fact, the uncertainty of the subject shares referred to by Shixin Ronghe Company concerned the Agreement on Performance Compensation signed by the listed company Century Guanghua with the asset restructuring party Hengyi Group, Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo to protect the interests of minority shareholders. The content was that if Zhejiang Hengyi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. under the agreement failed to meet the agreed profit targets in any accounting year, Century Guanghua could repurchase the shares held by Hengyi Group, Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo at a price of 1 yuan per share, with the aim of reducing the registered capital of "Hengyi Petrochemical" to improve corporate performance and protect the interests of minority shareholders. The compensation agreement also stipulated that if the performance compensation situation under the agreement occurred, Century Guanghua would first repurchase shares from Hengyi Group; if the number of shares of Century Guanghua held by Hengyi Group was less than the number of compensation shares, Century Guanghua would repurchase shares from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo held by the two parties. However, during the entire execution period of the trust plan, Century Guanghua did not repurchase the shares held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, and the uncertainty alleged by Shixin Ronghe Company did not occur. The termination of the trust contracts was entirely due to the trustee Chang'an Trust, in accordance with the contract provisions, liquidating and cashing out the subject shares after they fell below the guaranteed price for priority beneficiaries, based on instructions from the priority beneficiaries. This was purely a commercial risk stipulated in the contracts and was not caused by any uncertainty affecting the execution of the trust contracts. Third, the trust property in this case should be determined. Shixin Ronghe Company's belief that the trust property was uncertain was a misunderstanding of the law. Article 2 of the Trust Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Trust Law) provides: "For the purposes of this Law, trust refers to an act in which the settlor, based on trust in the trustee, entrusts his property rights to the trustee, and the trustee manages or disposes of the property in his own name according to the settlor's wishes, for the benefit of the beneficiary or for a specific purpose." Article 7 provides: "To establish a trust, there must be definite trust property, and the trust property must be property lawfully owned by the settlor. For the purposes of this Law, property includes lawful property rights." Article 14 provides: "The property acquired by the trustee as a result of accepting the trust is trust property. Property acquired by the trustee through the management, use, disposal, or other circumstances of the trust property also becomes part of the trust property." At the time Chang'an Trust and Shixin Ronghe Company entered into the trust contracts, the trust contracts clearly defined the trustee and the settlor: the trustee was Chang'an Trust, the settlor was Dongfang Gaosheng, and the beneficiary and the settlor were the same person. Based on the provisions of the contracts and a correct understanding of the above legal provisions, the trust property in this case should be the funds of 112,031,000 yuan delivered by the settlor Dongfang Gaosheng to the trustee Chang'an Trust, not the Hengyi Petrochemical shares purchased with the trust funds of 112,031,000 yuan from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo. Therefore, the trust property was determined. Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo were not settlors in the trust legal relationship of this case; the shares they held and transferred to Chang'an Trust constituted a sales legal relationship, not a trust legal relationship. The subject matter of their transfer was not trust property, and whether that subject matter was determined did not affect the legal relationship of the trust contracts. In summary, Shixin Ronghe Company's request to confirm the invalidity of the trust contracts on the ground that the trust property was uncertain lacked both factual and legal basis, and the court did not support it; its claims should be dismissed. The court, in accordance with Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Article 8 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 68 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC, Articles 2 and 14 of the Trust Law, and Articles 148 and 152 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered a judgment dismissing Shixin Ronghe Company's claims. The litigation costs of 740,750 yuan were to be borne by Shixin Ronghe Company.

Shixin Ronghe Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment, appealed to this Court, requesting that the judgment be set aside and the case be retried or remanded for a new trial, with litigation costs to be borne by Chang'an Trust, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Dinghui Management Center. The reasons were: 1. The original trial judgment erred in finding that the trust property in this case was determined. The trust property in this case was not determined, and the two involved Trust Contracts were invalid. (i) The original trial judgment incorrectly identified the trust property in this case. It found that the trust property was the 112,031,000 yuan funds paid by Dongfang Gaosheng to Chang'an Trust, which was inconsistent with the legislative intent of the Trust Law. Under Article 14 of that Law, trust property includes not only property acquired by the trustee as a result of accepting the trust, but also property acquired through the management, use, disposal, or other circumstances of the trust property. In this case, because Dongfang Gaosheng delivered the trust funds to Chang'an Trust and thereby acquired the earnings rights of the subject shares, the trust property had been transformed from trust funds into the earnings rights of the subject shares. Accordingly, in determining whether the trust property was determined, the analysis should focus on whether the earnings rights of the subject shares were determined. The original trial judgment's reliance on the certainty of the trust funds to find the trust property determined was erroneous. (ii) The determination of trust property should be the determination of its "ownership." In this case, the Agreement on Performance Compensation signed by Hengyi Group, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Century Guanghua imposed a burden on the rights of the subject shares, with a possibility that the subject shares might be repurchased by Century Guanghua. The Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement and Stock Pledge Contract signed by Chang'an Trust with Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo could hinder such repurchase and thereby harm the interests of public shareholders, so there was a possibility that the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement might be invalid. Because of the potential repurchase of the subject shares and the possible invalidity of the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement, the ownership of the subject shares in this case was uncertain, and accordingly, the earnings rights of the subject shares, as one of the components of ownership, were also uncertain. (iii) The original trial judgment's denial of the uncertainty of the trust property based on the fact that the subject shares were ultimately not repurchased was untenable. The fact that the subject shares were not actually repurchased could not cure the uncertainty of the trust property, specifically the earnings rights of the subject shares. 2. Chang'an Trust and Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo acted in malicious collusion, harming the interests of Dongfang Gaosheng. The Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement should be invalid, and the foundation for establishing the trust was lost, so the two involved Trust Contracts should also be invalid. In the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement, Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo warranted that there were no legal or factual circumstances affecting the transfer of the stock earnings rights or the disposal of the subject shares. In fact, Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo failed to disclose the fact that they were obligated to repurchase the subject shares. Moreover, because this fact was publicly disclosed by the listed company Century Guanghua, Chang'an Trust, as a professional financial investment company, could not have been unaware of the repurchase obligation on the subject shares when it subsequently signed the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement. The above circumstances indicated that Chang'an Trust and Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo colluded to conceal the fact that the rights to the subject shares were uncertain, which not only violated the provisions of the Trust Law and other laws and regulations but also caused Dongfang Gaosheng to sign the involved Trust Contracts with Chang'an Trust without knowing the fact of the uncertain rights on the subject shares, thereby harming the interests of Dongfang Gaosheng. Therefore, the Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement between Chang'an Trust and Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo should be invalid. Accordingly, the two involved Trust Contracts between Dongfang Gaosheng and Chang'an Trust should also be invalid. Additionally, the original trial judgment's finding that the two involved Trust Contracts represented the true intentions of Dongfang Gaosheng simply because they were proposed by Dongfang Gaosheng was untenable. 3. The original trial judgment found some facts without cross-examination, and there were some textual errors. (i) The facts found by the original trial judgment included: the letter of inquiry sent by Chang'an Trust to Dongfang Gaosheng on March 7, 2013, and Dongfang Gaosheng's seal of approval; the trust instruction issued by the Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. to Chang'an Trust on September 26, 2014; and the Notice Letter sent by Chang'an Trust to Dongfang Gaosheng on October 11, 2014. These facts were not subjected to cross-examination. (ii) As for textual errors: the consideration for Century Guanghua's repurchase of shares from the restructuring parties was a total price of 1 yuan, not "1 yuan per share" as stated in the original trial judgment; the subject shares were "Hengyi Petrochemical," not "Hengyi Petrochemical" as stated in the original trial judgment; the transaction should be "T day," not "T day" as stated in the original trial judgment, etc.

Chang'an Trust argued in its defense: The original trial judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. The reasons were: 1. Shixin Ronghe Company misunderstood the concept of trust property that must have "determinacy." The provisions of Articles 7, 11, and 14 of the Trust Law showed that the "determinacy" of trust property was only required at the time of the establishment of the trust; during the execution phase after establishment, no "determinacy" was required. In this case, the trust funds of 112,031,000 yuan established under the trust were determined. 2. In this case, the loss of Chang'an Trust's property was caused by normal risks under the trust, and this loss had nothing to do with any uncertainty in the ownership of the subject shares. 3. There was no "uncertainty" in the ownership of the subject shares. (i) Chang'an Trust had already established a pledge over the subject shares, and this in rem right took precedence over Century Guanghua's right of repurchase, which was a contractual right. (ii) The repurchase right held by Century Guanghua over the subject shares was essentially a compensation to the minority shareholders of Century Guanghua. Even if a repurchase occurred, Dinghui Phase I, etc., could purchase the corresponding number of shares on the market to satisfy the repurchase requirement, which would not lead to uncertainty of the subject shares. (iii) In this case, no repurchase actually occurred. 4. Dongfang Gaosheng knew the public fact that Century Guanghua could repurchase the subject shares, so Chang'an Trust and Dinghui Phase I, etc., did not have malicious collusion. Moreover, in this case, the purpose of Dongfang Gaosheng's establishment was precisely to invest in the subject shares, and the involved trust was actively promoted by Dongfang Gaosheng. The legal representative of Shixin Ronghe Company, the main partner of Dongfang Gaosheng, directly presided over the investment meeting. Shixin Ronghe Company filed this lawsuit to shift the risk. 5. The facts that Shixin Ronghe Company claimed were not cross-examined pertained to the performance of the two involved Trust Contracts, which was irrelevant to the validity of the Trust Contracts in dispute. Those facts did not affect the outcome of the original trial judgment.

Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Dinghui Management Center jointly argued in their defense: The original trial judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. The reasons were: 1. The subject shares and their earnings rights held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo were the objects of purchase with trust funds, not the trust property itself. Therefore, whether those earnings rights might be repurchased did not affect the determinacy of the trust property. The involved Stock Earnings Rights Transfer Agreement and the Trust Contracts were both valid. 2. Shixin Ronghe Company was not a counterparty to the transactions of Dinghui Phase I or Dinghui Yuanbo, and it had no right to file a lawsuit against Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, or Dinghui Management Center.

Dongfang Gaosheng stated that it agreed with the opinions of Chang'an Trust, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Dinghui Management Center.

Shixin Ronghe Company objected to the following facts found by the original trial: the letter of inquiry sent by Chang'an Trust to Dongfang Gaosheng on March 7, 2013, and Dongfang Gaosheng's seal of approval; the trust instruction issued by the Shanghai Branch of Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. to Chang'an Trust on September 26, 2014; and the Notice Letter sent by Chang'an Trust to Dongfang Gaosheng on October 11, 2014. This Court affirms the other facts found by the original trial judgment.

This Court further finds: 1. Dinghui Management Center is the general partner of the two partnership enterprises Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo. 2. Regarding the textual errors in the original trial judgment identified by Shixin Ronghe Company, Chang'an Trust, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, Dinghui Management Center, and Dongfang Gaosheng all acknowledged them.

This Court is of the opinion: The funds of 112,031,000 yuan delivered by Dongfang Gaosheng to Chang'an Trust for the subscription of trust units under the two involved Trust Contracts are recognized by Shixin Ronghe Company, Chang'an Trust, and Dongfang Gaosheng as trust property under the aforementioned Trust Contracts. Therefore, this Court confirms that the 112,031,000 yuan funds constitute trust property acquired by the trustee Chang'an Trust. Property acquired by the trustee through the management, use, or disposal of trust property should also become part of the trust property. Since Chang'an Trust's acquisition of the earnings rights of the subject shares from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo using the above funds constituted the use of trust property, this Court supports Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the earnings rights of the subject shares acquired by Chang'an Trust also constitute trust property. The original trial judgment's finding that the earnings rights of the subject shares acquired by Chang'an Trust from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo were not trust property was inappropriate, and this Court hereby corrects it.

In a trust legal relationship, the certainty of trust property requires that the trust property be segregated and designated from the settlor's own property, and that its quantity and boundaries be clear. That is, the trust property must be definite and specific so that the trustee can manage, utilize, and dispose of it for the purpose of realizing the trust purpose. In this case, Chang'an Trust, Dinghui Phase I, and Dinghui Yuanbo respectively agreed in the corresponding "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" that the stock income rights include the disposal income from 9,003,983 shares held by Dinghui Phase I and 2,539,585 shares held by Dinghui Yuanbo, totaling 11,543,568 shares, as well as the dividends, bonus shares, rights offerings, new share warrants, and other fruits actually obtained from the stocks during the agreed income period. This agreement specified the quantity, content of rights, and boundaries of the stock income rights in dispute obtained by Chang'an Trust, thereby rendering the stock income rights in dispute acquired by Chang'an Trust definite and specific, and the trustee Chang'an Trust could fully manage and utilize such stock income rights. Therefore, regardless of whether the trust property was the funds of RMB 112,031,000 delivered by Dongfang Gaosheng to Chang'an Trust under the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute, or the stock income rights acquired by Chang'an Trust from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo using the aforesaid funds, it was all certain. Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the trust property under the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute was uncertain lacks a factual basis, and this Court does not support its claim.

Before Chang'an Trust acquired the stock income rights in dispute from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and others, in the "Agreement on Performance Compensation" signed with Shiji Guanghua, undertook that if the actual profits of Zhejiang Hengyi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. for the relevant fiscal year under the agreement failed to meet the target, Shiji Guanghua could repurchase the corresponding shares held by Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo. After the income rights of the aforesaid stocks were transferred to Chang'an Trust, the issue arising from the aforesaid undertaking was that if the actual profits of Zhejiang Hengyi Petrochemical Co., Ltd. for the relevant fiscal year failed to meet the target, the repurchase rights of Shiji Guanghua over the stocks in dispute would need to be reconciled with the income rights of Chang'an Trust. The issue of reconciling the rights and interests over the stocks in dispute and the issue of the certainty of the stock income rights are different legal issues with no legal connection between them. The reconciliation of rights and interests over the stocks in dispute can be resolved in accordance with legal provisions, and such reconciliation does not necessarily result in Chang'an Trust losing the stock income rights it acquired. In this case, because Chang'an Trust had already obtained a pledge over the stocks to secure the realization of the stock income rights, Chang'an Trust's rights over the stocks in dispute took priority over those of Shiji Guanghua. Moreover, in this case, Shiji Guanghua did not actually repurchase the stocks in dispute. Therefore, the stocks in dispute did not cause Chang'an Trust to be unable to possess the stock income rights due to repurchase by Shiji Guanghua. Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the "ownership" of the stocks in dispute was uncertain, and thus the stock income rights were also uncertain, essentially contends that Shiji Guanghua's repurchase rights over the stocks in dispute would prevent Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo from owning the "ownership" of the stocks, thereby preventing Chang'an Trust from enjoying the stock income rights. As discussed above, this claim lacks legal basis and is therefore untenable. The repurchase rights enjoyed by Shiji Guanghua over the stocks in dispute did not legally affect the stock income rights that constituted the trust property. Shixin Ronghe Company's argument that the existence of Shiji Guanghua's repurchase rights over the stocks in dispute should negate the validity of the "Trust Contracts" is insufficient in both fact and law, and this Court does not support it.

As there is no fact in this case that Shiji Guanghua was obstructed from repurchasing the stocks from Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo, Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Stock Pledge Contract" harmed the interests of public shareholders by obstructing Shiji Guanghua's repurchase of the stocks in dispute lacks a factual basis. Shixin Ronghe Company acknowledges that the repurchase rights of Shiji Guanghua over the stocks in dispute were publicly disclosed facts. Therefore, even if Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo did not specifically disclose the aforesaid facts in the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" signed with Chang'an Trust, this does not constitute malicious collusion to conceal the aforesaid facts. Moreover, the repurchase rights of Shiji Guanghua over the stocks in dispute did not, in fact, affect Chang'an Trust's actual acquisition of the stock income rights or disposal of the stocks. Therefore, when Dinghui Phase I and Dinghui Yuanbo stated in signing the aforesaid agreement with Chang'an Trust that there were no circumstances affecting the transfer of stock income rights or the disposal of the stocks in dispute, this statement was not improper, and the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" should not be held invalid on the grounds of malicious collusion harming the interests of a third party, Dongfang Gaosheng. Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the "Stock Income Rights Transfer Agreement" is invalid lacks sufficient factual basis and is difficult to sustain. Accordingly, Shixin Ronghe Company's argument that the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute are invalid based on the invalidity of that agreement is also untenable.

The matters found in the original trial judgment regarding Chang'an Trust sending an inquiry letter to Dongfang Gaosheng on March 7, 2013, and Dongfang Gaosheng affixing its seal in agreement; Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., Shanghai Branch issuing an entrusted instruction to Chang'an Trust on September 26, 2014; and Chang'an Trust sending a "Notice Letter" to Dongfang Gaosheng on October 11, 2014, are issues arising from the performance of the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute. As such issues do not affect the validity of the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute, this Court will not adjudicate them. Since there is no evidence in this case negating the validity of the two "Trust Contracts" in dispute, this Court does not accept Shixin Ronghe Company's claim that the contracts are invalid. Shixin Ronghe Company, based on the alleged invalidity of the aforesaid "Trust Contracts," claims that Chang'an Trust should return the subscription funds of RMB 112,031,000 and the deposit of RMB 6,065,814, plus corresponding interest, and that Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and their general partner, Dinghui Management Center, should bear joint and several liability. None of these claims can be sustained, and this Court does not support them. As for Shixin Ronghe Company's comments regarding clerical errors in the original trial judgment, this Court adopts them and hereby makes corrections.

In conclusion, the two "Trust Contracts" signed between Dongfang Gaosheng and Chang'an Trust in this case are valid. Shixin Ronghe Company's request, based on these "Trust Contracts," that Chang'an Trust, Dinghui Phase I, Dinghui Yuanbo, and Dinghui Management Center jointly and severally return the subscription funds, deposit, and corresponding interest cannot be sustained. The original trial judgment found the basic facts clearly, and although the application of law was improper, the result of the judgment was correct and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 740,750 shall be borne by Shixin Ronghe Investment Management Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
